description: Evrenin oluşumu hakkında bilgiler arayan bir kaşifim.
summary: Our project proposes a theory—similar to that of NASA scientist Dr. Nikodem Poplawski—suggesting that the universe is a black hole, or conversely, that black holes are universes. Our theory is supported by our own specific arguments: first, given that electrons absorb light and the outer layer of a black hole consists of electrons, we posit that this is why black holes appear black. The remaining components—protons and neutrons—reside within the core of the black hole, much like the structure of an atom. Between these two layers lies a region where gravitational forces reach equilibrium; we have termed this the "command axis" (emir ekseni), and according to our theory, galaxies are situated along this orbit. Furthermore, when accounting for the event horizon, it becomes evident that the density of a black hole is comparable to the density of the universe itself. Our theory is indirectly linked to the Big Bang model; for instance, the collision of two stars—a potential scenario within the Big Bang framework—can lead to the formation of a black hole. We argue that the rotation of a black hole is driven by the mutual repulsion of the electrons in its outer layer. Additionally, we propose that matter entering a black hole—having lost its stability—eventually escapes the immense pressure, reverting to its original state; once restored, these atoms settle along what we call the "command axis," where they remain in rotation.
details: Our project explores our ideas regarding the formation of the universe; by transforming these concepts into a theory, we have sought to shed light on the nature of black holes—thereby generating new knowledge—and to help clarify the model of the universe that people hold in their minds.
